question: What is the main problem that happens in the body during obstetric shock?

options.A: Rapid destruction of platelets in the blood
options.B: Sudden rise in pressure inside the head
options.C: Not enough blood flow reaching vital organs

explanation: Shock happens when the circulatory system fails to supply enough blood and oxygen to vital organs, causing cells to stop working properly. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why might a pregnant woman lose a lot of blood before her blood pressure actually drops?

options.A: The baby's heartbeat speeds up to make up for the blood loss
options.B: Pregnancy increases total blood volume, hiding early blood loss
options.C: Pregnancy hormones artificially stabilize blood pressure
options.D: The placenta acts as a backup tank to keep pressure steady

explanation: Because pregnancy increases total blood volume, the body compensates for initial bleeding, meaning blood pressure stays normal until shock is advanced. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which sign is usually the very first warning that a patient is developing shock from blood loss?
explanation: Tachycardia happens early because the heart pumps faster to make up for a drop in circulating blood volume. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h2)

question: A postpartum mother looks anxious, her skin is pale and sweaty, and her pulse is 120 beats per minute. What do these signs point to?
explanation: Anxiety, pale and sweaty skin, and a fast pulse are classic early warning signs of inadequate tissue perfusion and shock. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why should an unconscious pregnant woman in shock be placed with a tilt to her left side?

options.A: To keep her from swallowing her saliva
options.B: To stop the heavy uterus from pressing on major blood vessels
options.C: To help lochia drain out of the vagina
options.D: To make it easier to put in an IV line

explanation: Tilting the patient to the left relieves pressure off the aorta and inferior vena cava, keeping blood flowing back to the heart. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h3)

question: What size of intravenous cannula is best for quickly giving fluids in severe obstetric shock?
explanation: Large-bore cannulas allow rapid infusion of large volumes of fluids and blood products under pressure. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is a major danger of giving too much simple salt solution (crystalloid) during severe bleeding?

options.A: Causing a sudden allergic skin rash
options.B: Causing a sudden drop in body temperature
options.C: Diluting clotting factors and making bleeding worse

explanation: Too much crystalloid fluid dilutes the blood's natural clotting factors, making it harder for the body to stop bleeding. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the best type of fluid to replace blood when a patient has lost a dangerous amount of it?

options.B: Oral rehydration salts mixed in water

explanation: Replacing lost blood with actual blood or blood products restores oxygen-carrying capacity and clotting factors best. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why is it not enough to just treat the symptoms of shock in an emergency?

options.A: Patients will develop an allergy to the IV cannula
options.B: Resuscitation fluids cannot work without extra drugs
options.C: Blood pressure will rise too high if the root cause is ignored
options.D: The underlying cause will keep making the patient worse

explanation: If the source of bleeding, infection, or vascular spasm is not stopped, the patient will continue to lose ground despite fluid therapy. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which medication is crucial for managing a patient with severe pre-eclampsia who is at risk of having seizures?
explanation: Magnesium sulfate is the drug of choice for preventing and treating seizures associated with severe pre-eclampsia and eclampsia. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a recommended step when preparing a shocked obstetric patient for transport to another hospital?

options.A: Having a trained provider go along to monitor vitals
options.B: Sending a written record of all treatments given
options.C: Stopping all IV fluids so the bags do not spill
options.D: Making sure IV lines stay open and running

explanation: IV fluids and resuscitation must continue uninterrupted during transport to maintain stability; they should never be stopped. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why do midwives measure urine output every hour when resuscitating a patient in shock?

options.A: Good urine output shows that the kidneys and vital organs are getting enough blood flow
options.B: It proves the patient does not have a urinary tract infection
options.C: It shows that the bladder is empty and keeps the uterus in place
options.D: It proves that the IV fluids have no bacteria in them

explanation: The kidneys are sensitive to low blood volume and shut down early; seeing urine output return to normal confirms good systemic perfusion. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h6)
